notes:
Vectors

  • Triangle/parallelogram law: $R = \sqrt{A^2+B^2+2AB\cos\theta}$; direction $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{B\sin\theta}{A+B\cos\theta}$.
  • Resultant is maximum ($A+B$) when $\theta = 0^\circ$ and minimum ($|A-B|$) when $\theta = 180^\circ$. For two equal vectors of magnitude $A$ at angle $\theta$: $R = 2A\cos(\theta/2)$.
  • Resolution into components: $A_x = A\cos\theta$, $A_y = A\sin\theta$.
  • Dot product $\vec A\cdot\vec B = AB\cos\theta$ (scalar). Cross product $|\vec A\times\vec B| = AB\sin\theta$ (vector; direction by the right-hand rule).

Projectile motion (launch speed $u$, angle $\theta$ to horizontal)

  • Time of flight $T = \dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$
  • Maximum height $H = \dfrac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$
  • Range $R = \dfrac{u^2\sin2\theta}{g}$, maximum at $\theta = 45^\circ$, giving $R_{max} = u^2/g$; at $45^\circ$, $H = R/4$.
  • Same range for complementary angles $\theta$ and $(90^\circ-\theta)$.
  • Trajectory is a parabola: $y = x\tan\theta - \dfrac{gx^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$.
  • Horizontal projectile launched from height $h$: time to land $t = \sqrt{2h/g}$; horizontal range $= v_0t$.

Uniform circular motion

  • Speed is constant but the velocity direction (tangential to the circle) keeps changing, so the motion is accelerated.
  • Centripetal acceleration $a = \dfrac{v^2}{r} = \omega^2r$, always directed toward the centre.
  • $v = r\omega$; time period $T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{v} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$; frequency $n = 1/T$.

Exam tip

KCET typically sets about 2 questions from this chapter — usually one projectile range/height numerical and one vector-algebra or circular-motion concept/numerical. Most are a single direct substitution into the boxed formulas above.

questions.explanation: Range depends on $\sin2\theta$, which is the same for complementary angles $\theta$ and $(90^\circ-\theta)$; here $90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$.

questions.explanation: $y = x\tan\theta - \dfrac{gx^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$ is quadratic in $x$, i.e. a parabola.

A particle moves in a circle of radius 2 m with angular velocity 5 rad s$^{-1}$. Its linear speed is
In uniform circular motion, the instantaneous velocity of the particle is directed
questions.explanation: The velocity is always tangent to the circular path; only its direction (not magnitude) keeps changing.

questions.q: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration of the particle is directed
options: towards the centre of the circle
it is zero since speed is constant
away from the centre of the circle
questions.explanation: Even though speed is constant, velocity direction changes continuously, producing a centripetal acceleration directed towards the centre.

A unit vector is a vector whose
options: magnitude equals that of a given vector
questions.explanation: A unit vector has magnitude exactly 1 and is used only to indicate direction; $\hat n = \vec A/|\vec A|$.

questions.q: Rain falls vertically downward at 8 m s$^{-1}$. A man walks horizontally at 6 m s$^{-1}$. The magnitude of the velocity of rain relative to the man is
questions.explanation: $\vec v_{rain,man} = \vec v_{rain} - \vec v_{man}$, with perpendicular components 8 and 6: magnitude $=\sqrt{8^2+6^2}=\sqrt{100}=10$ m s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: For the situation above (rain falling at 8 m s$^{-1}$, man walking at 6 m s$^{-1}$), the man must hold his umbrella tilted from the vertical, towards his direction of motion, at an angle of about
A ball is projected with speed 20 m s$^{-1}$ at 60° to the horizontal. Its speed at the highest point of the trajectory is
questions.explanation: At the highest point only the horizontal component survives: $v = u\cos\theta = 20\times\cos60^\circ = 10$ m s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: A projectile is launched with speed 30 m s$^{-1}$ at 30° to the horizontal. The time taken to reach its maximum height is
If $\vec A = 4\hat i + 3\hat j$ and $\vec B = 2\hat i - 3\hat j$, the magnitude of $\vec A + \vec B$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec A+\vec B = 6\hat i + 0\hat j$, whose magnitude is $\sqrt{6^2+0^2} = 6$.

questions.q: Several vectors are added and their resultant turns out to be zero. This means that
options: all the vectors must be equal in magnitude
the vectors, placed head to tail, form a closed polygon
all the vectors must be parallel to each other
each vector must have zero magnitude
questions.explanation: A zero resultant only requires that the vectors, drawn head to tail in sequence, close up into a polygon; individual vectors need not be zero, equal, or parallel.

If $\vec A \cdot \vec B = 0$ and neither $\vec A$ nor $\vec B$ is a null vector, the angle between them is
questions.explanation: $\vec A\cdot\vec B = AB\cos\theta = 0$ with $A,B\neq0$ requires $\cos\theta = 0$, i.e. $\theta = 90^\circ$.

questions.q: If $\vec A \times \vec B = \vec 0$ for two non-zero vectors, they must be
questions.explanation: $|\vec A\times\vec B| = AB\sin\theta = 0$ with $A,B\neq0$ requires $\sin\theta=0$, i.e. $\theta = 0^\circ$ or $180^\circ$.

questions.q: A boat can move at 4 m s$^{-1}$ in still water. It heads straight across a river flowing at 3 m s$^{-1}$, perpendicular to its heading. The boat's resultant speed relative to the ground is
questions.explanation: The two velocities are perpendicular, so $v_{resultant}=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}=\sqrt{25}=5$ m s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: For the boat above (still-water speed 4 m s$^{-1}$ heading straight across a 100 m wide river flowing at 3 m s$^{-1}$), the downstream drift when it reaches the opposite bank is
questions.explanation: Time to cross $= 100/4 = 25$ s (only the perpendicular component matters). Drift $=$ flow speed $\times$ time $= 3\times25 = 75$ m.

questions.q: The velocity vector of a projectile at the highest point of its trajectory makes an angle with the horizontal equal to
options: equal to the angle of projection
questions.explanation: At the highest point the vertical velocity component is zero, so the velocity is purely horizontal, i.e. at $0^\circ$ to the horizontal.

questions.q: Two vectors of equal magnitude act on a particle in exactly opposite directions. Their resultant is
options: a vector of twice the magnitude
questions.explanation: For antiparallel equal vectors, $R=\sqrt{A^2+A^2+2A^2\cos180^\circ}=\sqrt{2A^2-2A^2}=0$, the null vector.
